heading: Flagship Engineering Systems
intro: Production trading infrastructure, low-latency distribution pipelines, and architectural case studies.

flagship_systems.title: High-Throughput Algorithmic Trading & Backtesting Engine
flagship_systems.context: Backtesting multi-strategy models across 50 instruments over 3 years of 1-minute OHLCV data created severe memory overhead and Garbage Collector allocation pauses in traditional object-oriented pipeline designs.
constraints: Eliminating .NET Garbage Collector pauses under sustained multi-million candle workloads
Zero-copy sharing of historical price feeds across concurrent strategy instances
Maintaining a deterministic unmanaged interop bridge between C++ and .NET runtimes
flagship_systems.architecture_summary: Engineered a zero-copy data pipeline using memory-mapped files and blittable value types. Shared technical indicators compute once on a vector bus and stream into concurrent strategy evaluation pipelines with modular exit rules.

decisions.title: Memory-Mapped File Storage
decisions.detail: Directly maps multi-gigabyte historical market datasets into process memory without loading entire arrays into the managed heap.

decisions.title: Blittable Struct Memory Layout
decisions.detail: Sequential memory representations for price ticks and order events, eliminating boxing/unboxing overhead and reducing RAM footprint by ~80%.

decisions.title: Shared Indicator Computation Bus
decisions.detail: Vectorized calculation of indicators (ATR, moving averages, volatility bands) executed once and reused across all active strategy instances.

evidence.label: 50 symbols × 3 years × 1-minute OHLCV full pipeline backtest completed in under 3 minutes.

flagship_systems.title: Low-Latency Market Data Distribution Pipeline
flagship_systems.context: Real-time distribution of high-frequency tick and quote market feeds to hundreds of distributed client applications with sub-10ms delivery requirements.
constraints: Preventing network buffer congestion under sudden market volatility bursts
Managing hundreds of concurrent client connections with minimal serialization overhead
Providing a deterministic bridge from low-level TCP sockets to web dashboard consumers
flagship_systems.architecture_summary: Engineered a low-level multi-threaded socket listener with custom binary packet framing feeding an in-memory ring buffer. Decoupled socket ingestion from client broadcasting via dedicated SignalR hubs.

decisions.title: Low-Level Socket Programming
decisions.detail: Direct TCP socket management bypassing heavy framework abstractions to ensure deterministic packet handling.

decisions.title: Producer-Consumer Ring Buffer
decisions.detail: Lock-free memory ring buffer decouples network ingress from client fan-out broadcasting.

decisions.title: SignalR Web Distribution Bridge
decisions.detail: Streams normalized market tick and quote updates to web dashboards with low transport latency.

evidence.label: Tick and quote market data published to hundreds of clients with sub-10ms delivery delay.

flagship_systems.title: Dynamic Cloud Trading Migration & Infrastructure Optimization
flagship_systems.context: Legacy cloud-based trading execution infrastructure faced escalating operating costs and operational overhead as multi-asset strategies expanded.
constraints: Zero downtime or trade execution disruption during infrastructure transition
Maintaining strict low-latency execution guarantees while eliminating idle provisioning waste
flagship_systems.architecture_summary: Designed and deployed a dynamic migration system tailoring compute allocation to strategy volatility and trading session hours.

decisions.title: Dynamic Resource Scheduling
decisions.detail: Automated scaling aligned with global market sessions and strategy compute intensity.

decisions.title: Resource & Memory Profiling
decisions.detail: Eliminated idle cloud resource wastage, resulting in a verified 98.8% operational cost reduction while improving support efficiency.

evidence.label: Operational cost reduction achieved while improving support efficiency and deployment reliability.
